prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Pleasanton California?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for everyone—“best” depends on the type of case (car crash, slip and fall, medical malpractice, workplace injury), how serious the injury is, whether you want a trial lawyer, fee structure, and your priorities (highest settlement, fast resolution, local convenience, bilingual, etc.).

To help you pick, I can either (A) give guidance on how to evaluate lawyers and what questions to ask, or (B) search and return a short vetted list of top-rated personal injury lawyers or firms that handle cases in Pleasanton. Which would you prefer?

If you want immediate help deciding, here are quick pointers and next steps:

What to consider when choosing
- Relevant experience: years handling the specific type of personal injury you have and trial experience if your case may go to court.  
- Track record: recent verdicts/settlements for similar cases.  
- Reputation and credentials: peer ratings (Martindale‑Hubbell AV, Super Lawyers), local bar involvement, client reviews.  
- Fees and communication: contingency fee percentage, who pays costs, whether they give free consults, how often they’ll update you.  
- Availability and responsiveness: who will actually handle your file (partner vs. associate).  
- Disciplinary history: check the State Bar of California for any records.

Important practical items
- Statute of limitations: in California most personal injury claims must be filed within 2 years of the injury. Medical malpractice has different deadlines (often 1 year from discovery, with a 3‑year outer limit). Don’t delay contacting an attorney.  
- Preserve evidence and records: photos, medical records, police reports, witness contacts.

If you want me to find options now, tell me:
- What type of injury/claim is it? (car crash, slip & fall, medical, product liability, etc.)  
- Do you want attorneys located specifically in Pleasanton or is Alameda/Contra Costa/San Jose area OK?  
- Any other preferences (trial lawyer, bilingual, contingency only)?

I can then return a short list (3–5) with contact info, ratings, and why each might fit your case.
